subject: Efficiency of multi-level normal model with known covariance -- Cholesky tricks

messages.author: f17ec5a3936c7373
messages.subject: Efficiency of multi-level normal model with known covariance -- Cholesky tricks
parts:
Hi STAN community,

I am working with a multi-level normal model where some random effects ('batch' and 'strain_*_indep') are independent and the others ('strain_*_add') have known a known covariance.

Some notes on the terminology I'm using here, that may make this model easier to read...
"phenotype" is the genetics term for what most would call "response" or "depdendent variable". 
"mef" is my shorthand for "mean effect", or said another way "effect on the mean of the phenotype" or "effect on the expected value of the phenotype"
"vef" is my shorthand for "variance effect", or said another way "effect on the variance of the phenotype".  Because of the way this model is parametrized, "vef"s are actually effects on the log of the standard deviation of the phenotype....but conceptually they relate to variance.
Effects that end with "_indep" have the identity matrix as their covariance, so are modeled with 'normal()'
Effects that end with "_add" have a known covariance matrix determined by the genetics of the organisms.

data {
  int<lower = 0> num_obs;
  vector[num_obs] phenotype;
  
  int<lower = 1> num_batches;
  int<lower = 1, upper = num_batches> batch[num_obs];
  
  int<lower = 1> num_strains;
  int<lower = 1, upper = num_strains> strain[num_obs];
  
  vector[num_strains] strain_mef_add_mean;
  cov_matrix[num_strains] strain_mef_add_covar;
  
  vector[num_strains] strain_vef_add_mean;
  cov_matrix[num_strains] strain_vef_add_covar;
}

transformed data {
  cholesky_factor_cov[num_strains] strain_mef_add_chol;
  cholesky_factor_cov[num_strains] strain_vef_add_chol;
  
  strain_mef_add_chol = cholesky_decompose(strain_mef_add_covar);
  strain_vef_add_chol = cholesky_decompose(strain_vef_add_covar);
}

parameters {
  real mean_baseline;
  vector[num_batches] batch_mef_indep;
  real<lower = 0> sigma_batch_mef_indep;
  vector[num_strains] strain_mef_indep;
  real<lower = 0> sigma_strain_mef_indep;
  vector[num_strains] strain_mef_add;
  real<lower = 0> sigma_strain_mef_add;
  
  real log_sd_baseline;
  vector[num_batches] batch_vef_indep;
  real<lower = 0> sigma_batch_vef_indep;
  vector[num_strains] strain_vef_indep;
  real<lower = 0> sigma_strain_vef_indep;
  vector[num_strains] strain_vef_add;
  real<lower = 0> sigma_strain_vef_add;
}

transformed parameters {
  vector[num_obs] linear_predictor_mean;
  vector[num_obs] linear_predictor_log_sd;
  vector[num_obs] linear_predictor_sd;
  
  linear_predictor_mean = mean_baseline + batch_mef_indep[batch] + strain_mef_indep[strain] + strain_mef_add[strain];
  linear_predictor_log_sd = log_sd_baseline + batch_vef_indep[batch] + strain_vef_indep[strain] + strain_vef_add[strain];
  linear_predictor_sd = exp(linear_predictor_log_sd);
}

model {
  # variance component priors
  sigma_batch_mef_indep ~ cauchy(0, 1);
  sigma_strain_mef_indep ~ cauchy(0, 1);
  sigma_strain_mef_add ~ cauchy(0, 1);
  
  sigma_batch_vef_indep ~ cauchy(0, 1);
  sigma_strain_vef_indep ~ cauchy(0, 1);
  sigma_strain_vef_add ~ cauchy(0, 1);
  
  # components of mean model
  mean_baseline ~ normal(0, 100);
  batch_mef_indep ~ normal(0, sigma_batch_mef_indep);
  strain_mef_indep ~ normal(0, sigma_strain_mef_indep);
  strain_mef_add ~ multi_normal_cholesky(strain_mef_add_mean, sigma_strain_mef_add*strain_mef_add_chol);
  
  # components of variance model
  log_sd_baseline ~ normal(0, 100);
  batch_vef_indep ~ normal(0, sigma_batch_vef_indep);
  strain_vef_indep ~ normal(0, sigma_strain_vef_indep);
  strain_vef_add ~ multi_normal_cholesky(strain_vef_add_mean, sigma_strain_vef_add*strain_vef_add_chol);
  
  # central model
  phenotype ~ normal(linear_predictor_mean, linear_predictor_sd);
}


Questions:
  1. Here, 'strain_mef_add_mean' and 'strain_vef_add_mean' are data.  I always pass in a vector of zeros.  Is there a better way to do this?  For example, in R it's 'rep(0, n)'.  In python it's 'numpy.zeros(n)'.
  2. Is this the best way to handle sampling from a normal with known covariance?  There's extensive discussion in a previous thread, but it was four years ago, so I don't know how best practices may have changed.  I also saw some discussion of this topic in Sorenson, Hohstein, and Vasishth, 2016. But, because I don't know what 'multi_normal_cholesky' does under the hood, I don't know if the gains from the "Cholesky tricks" they describe are already baked into my model.  

Thanks for any suggestion or advice you can offer,

Robert Corty

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Efficiency of multi-level normal model with known covariance -- Cholesky tricks
parts:
(1) rep_vector(0, N) (or rep_row_vector, or rep_matrix, etc.)
creates a vector of 0 values. Best to define it as a variable in
transformed_data so it is only built once and reused.

(2) Yes, that's the best way to implement it, at least as far as I know.
If it has block structure, then you want to decompose into smaller
problems, but otherwise, I don't think there's a more efficient approach.

- Bob
